description: HomeTube is a friendly video downloader managing single video URL into organized content structure for automatic home media server experience.

sources.entry: HomeTube ⚠ - Web UI to download videos and playlists from 1700+ sites into a Plex or Jellyfin library, with quality selection, SponsorBlock sponsor removal, subtitles, clip cutting and resilient playlist sync. (Source Code) AGPL-3.0 Python/Docker

summary.one_liner: HomeTube is a Streamlit web UI that downloads single videos and playlists (via yt-dlp) and files them into a folder structure that Plex, Jellyfin or Emby can watch, with optional SponsorBlock sponsor removal.
summary.what_it_does: HomeTube provides a web interface where you paste a video or playlist URL and it downloads the best available quality using yt-dlp, then moves the file to a chosen destination folder with well-named files for media server libraries. It offers quality profiles and download strategies (auto best, best only, choose profile, choose format) and can be configured to use cookies from a file or local browser. SponsorBlock support detects and marks sponsor segments on YouTube, with management in the UI. Playlist sync tracks videos by ID, supports filename patterns with placeholders, detects renames and reorders, and can archive removed entries into an Archives folder. It also offers clip cutting, subtitle embedding, format conversion, audio extraction, custom yt-dlp arguments, and an optional Jellyfin library refresh notification. The README also describes a newer separate engine called Content, which is a different project surface sharing the same idea.
use_cases: download YouTube videos into a Plex or Jellyfin library
archive and sync YouTube playlists locally
remove sponsors from downloaded YouTube videos
cut clips from online videos for a home media server
batch download videos to a homelab NAS
save videos from many sites with yt-dlp via a web UI
how_to_run: python -m venv hometube-env && source hometube-env/bin/activate && pip install ".[local]"
notable: Moves finished downloads into media-server-friendly folder layouts for Plex, Jellyfin or Emby
Playlist sync tracks videos by ID, detects renames and reorders, and can archive removed videos
Quality selection analyzes available codecs and tries up to two profiles
SponsorBlock integration with UI-managed sponsor segments
Custom yt-dlp arguments can be set per download or globally via environment variable
caveats: Cookies are described as highly recommended and needed for reliable downloads; cookies file or browser extraction must be set up
Browser cookie extraction does not work natively inside Docker, per the README
Test coverage is stated as 22% of statements; the README also promotes a separate hosted service and a newer engine called Content
